role.altitude: The bookkeeper stops keying invoices and works on what the rules could not settle. They own the AFAS match rules, tolerances, VAT-code mappings and the supplier master data (IBAN, KvK, g-rekening). Within limits the Controller sets, they decide which suppliers and invoice types may post without anyone touching them. The job becomes more expert: less typing, more judgement on exceptions, tax treatment and data quality.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: the first round of reminders and the payment-status answers to customers (learn the dunning policy, how to talk to customers, when a dispute needs escalating)
Accountant: month-end accruals for goods received but not invoiced, and balance-sheet reconciliations of creditors, debtors and bank (learn accrual logic and the close calendar)
Payroll Specialist: checking agency hours against the wage-tax part paid into the g-rekening (learn ketenaansprakelijkheid and how the agency portals hold their data)
People Analytics and HRIS Analyst: keeping the AFAS supplier and cost-centre master data clean for Power BI (learn the data model and the nightly extract)
role.ceiling_note: Each FTE has about 1,600 hours a year. The eight tasks here cover about 31% of them (about 500 hours per FTE). The approval gates stay manual, and so do PDF suppliers, agency invoices and anything that needs a phone call. The top teams in APQC's benchmark handle more than 20,000 invoices per FTE a year, so the limit is how many exceptions come in and how clean the supplier data is, not hours spent keying. Payment approval and posting rights stay with people under the four-eyes principle and the auditor's expectations.
skills_to_grow: Designing AFAS match rules and tolerances, and reading the match statistics
Supplier master-data hygiene: IBAN-name check results, KvK, VAT numbers, g-rekening
Dutch VAT and reverse charge, and the coming e-invoicing and ViDA reporting deadlines
Ketenaansprakelijkheid (inlenersaansprakelijkheid) checks on the staffing agencies
Reviewing AI suggestions critically and logging exceptions so the rules can be improved
Basic Power BI and Excel Power Query for exception dashboards
role.ambitious_version: Run procure-to-pay as a daily close. UBL and matched invoices post overnight, agency invoices are checked against hours from the portals and the g-rekening share is split automatically, and the bookkeepers work an exception queue each morning. They also run a weekly cash and supplier-terms report for the FP&A Analysts and site managers, which shortens days to close and gives the forecast real payables and receivables data.

tasks.short: Enter purchase and sales invoices and bookings in AFAS, keep the ledgers current

today.trigger: Invoices arrive in the AP mailbox (PDF, some UBL), agency invoices come from the portals, and sales invoices are created from orders
steps: Open the PDF or UBL in AFAS Scan & herken
Check or type the supplier, amounts, VAT and order number
Fix fields the scan read wrong
Send the invoice for approval by email, or post it once approved
File the PDF and update the Excel side lists
today.time_sinks: PDF invoices from small suppliers and the three agencies, and approvals that sit in mailboxes

lenses.faster: UBL invoices and one-to-one matches with an order or receipt post and approve themselves in AFAS. A model reads the remaining PDFs into an e-invoice, and the bookkeeper only checks the fields it flags.
lenses.autonomous: An invoice arriving in the AP mailbox starts the flow. AFAS reads it, finds the supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN, and matches it to the order. Unmatched or low-confidence invoices wait in a queue for the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: A new service to the site managers in Rotterdam, Tilburg and Venlo: a daily view of their open purchase invoices and pending approvals, instead of month-end surprises. Demand would grow if it were cheaper, because managers now only ask when something is stuck.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss retyping PDF lines. The bookkeepers want more time to fix the cause of repeat errors, such as asking a supplier to send UBL.
lenses.options: Little to choose here. The one real choice is per supplier: ask them to send UBL, or keep reading their PDFs.
lenses.altitude: Their week becomes a morning exception queue plus supplier onboarding. They decide which suppliers are trusted for automatic posting, within limits the Controller sets.
reach: Accountant: booking month-end accruals for goods received but not invoiced (learn accrual rules)

tasks.human_edge: Recognising an invoice that is technically correct but wrong in context: a duplicate under a new number, a supplier whose bank details changed, a charge for work the site never ordered.
tasks.pattern_why: UBL and one-to-one matches are already rules in AFAS. The remaining work is turning messy PDFs into fields someone can check, which is a single model call inside a fixed flow.

in_practice.trigger: New invoice in the AP mailbox or an agency portal
steps: AFAS imports UBL directly; PDFs go through capture
The model extracts the header and lines and proposes the supplier from KvK, VAT number and IBAN
AFAS matches against the order or receipt and auto-approves exact matches
Exceptions land in the bookkeeper's queue with the reason
The bookkeeper corrects and confirms; the correction feeds the supplier template
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper confirms every PDF-captured invoice that is unmatched or has low confidence. Approval for payment stays with the budget holder.
data_needed: Supplier master data (KvK, VAT number, IBAN)
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS workflow history per invoice, with the source document attached

evidence.claim: AFAS Profit 8 reads UBL and PDF invoices to line level, and posts and approves one-to-one matches with an order or receipt
AFAS scans a PDF without UBL into an e-invoice and finds the supplier by KvK, VAT number and IBAN; gaps are filled by hand
Escalante Golf went from 2.5 minutes to 45 seconds per invoice with AI capture in NetSuite
70% of Dutch respondents still approve invoices on paper or by email

risks: The share of invoices that post without anyone touching them may stay low, because of supplier-specific ledger accounts and VAT exceptions
Errors in supplier master data spread straight into automatic postings
Agency invoices stay messy PDFs that do not match the hours
research_questions: What share of Noordhaven's invoices arrives as UBL today, and from which suppliers?
What one-to-one match rate does AFAS reach on Noordhaven's purchase orders and receipts in a pilot month?
How many minutes per PDF invoice does capture save after the bookkeeper's review?

tasks.short: Check invoices and postings for correct amounts, VAT codes, cost centres and ledger accounts

today.trigger: Before posting or paying an invoice, and before month-end close
steps: Recalculate totals and VAT on the invoice
Check the VAT code against supplier country and type
Check the ledger account and cost centre (site)
Look for duplicates in AFAS
Correct and repost errors
drudgery: Correcting codes after the Controller finds them at close
today.time_sinks: Errors found late at month-end that need a reversal and a new posting

lenses.faster: Validation rules check every posting on arrival: totals, VAT code against supplier country, reverse charge, duplicate number and amount, and valid cost centre. The bookkeeper only looks at the flags.
lenses.autonomous: Each new posting runs through the checks. Clean ones pass, and flagged ones go to the bookkeeper with the rule that fired.
lenses.ambitious: Checks every posting the day it arrives instead of at month-end. This cuts the Controller's audit adjustments, and demand would grow because cheaper checks can cover the sales side too.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss recalculating VAT. The bookkeepers want more time on the odd cases, such as reverse charge and intra-EU purchases, where knowledge counts.
lenses.options: Little here. The choice is the tolerance level per rule, which the Controller sets.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper maintains the rule set and its tolerances and reviews false positives. That is a more expert job.
reach: Controller: proposing VAT-code and posting rules for the close checklist (learn audit expectations)

tasks.human_edge: Judging whether a flagged deviation is a real error or a legitimate exception, for example a one-off reverse-charge service or a split across two sites.
tasks.pattern_why: Arithmetic, VAT-code logic and duplicate checks can be written down as rules and run without a model.

in_practice.trigger: An invoice or journal posted in AFAS
steps: Recalculate totals and VAT
Check the VAT code against supplier country and reverse-charge flag
Check for duplicates on supplier, number, amount and date
Validate ledger account and cost centre combinations
Send flagged items to the queue with the reason
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper resolves each flag. The Controller approves rule and tolerance changes.
data_needed: Chart of accounts and cost centres
in_practice.logs_to: Exception log in AFAS, with a monthly summary in Power BI

evidence.claim: Own ledger accounts, VAT codes and exceptions per administration are the main blockers for invoices that post without anyone touching them
Buyers may have to report intra-EU and reverse-charge purchases within 5 days of receipt under ViDA
Validation rules for VAT and duplicates are standard ERP functionality

risks: Too many false positives and people start ignoring the flags
Rules drift as the chart of accounts changes
research_questions: How many audit adjustments last year came from wrong VAT codes or cost centres?
What false-positive rate do duplicate checks give on Noordhaven's supplier data?
Can AFAS run these checks natively, or do they need an external script on the AFAS API?

tasks.short: Assign ledger account, cost centre, site and VAT code to each invoice per our coding rules

today.trigger: An invoice without a purchase order, or with an order that does not specify the coding
steps: Read the invoice description
Look up how this supplier was coded before
Choose the ledger account, cost centre and VAT code
Ask the site or budget holder if unclear
Enter the coding in AFAS
drudgery: Emailing sites about what an invoice is for
today.time_sinks: Invoices without a purchase order (fuel, repairs, utilities) and new suppliers

lenses.faster: A model suggests the coding from supplier history and the invoice text. The bookkeeper confirms or corrects it in one screen, and fixed suppliers get a fixed template.
lenses.autonomous: Capture of an invoice without a purchase order starts it. The model proposes coding with a confidence score, and the bookkeeper confirms each one.
lenses.ambitious: Codes repair and maintenance invoices to the asset or vehicle for the first time, so the transport team gets a cost-per-vehicle view. Demand would grow as the coding gets cheaper.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss searching old bookings. The bookkeepers want more time to agree on clear coding with the sites.
lenses.options: Little; the coding has one right answer per policy.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the coding templates per supplier and decides when a supplier moves to automatic coding.
reach: FP&A Analyst: tagging costs to budget lines and vehicles for forecasts (learn the budget structure)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing what a site actually bought and why. A repair can be maintenance or an investment, and that decides the balance sheet.
tasks.pattern_why: The input is free invoice text and the output is a checkable code combination, so one model call inside the AFAS flow fits.

in_practice.trigger: Invoice without a purchase order captured in AFAS
steps: Send the invoice text and supplier history to the model
Receive the proposed ledger account, cost centre, VAT code and a reason
Show the proposal in the AFAS queue
The bookkeeper confirms or corrects
Store corrections in the supplier template
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper confirms each coding before posting; capital-versus-expense questions go to the Accountant.
data_needed: 12 months of coded invoices per supplier
Chart of accounts and cost centres
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS posting history, with the proposed and the final coding stored

evidence.claim: Coding is suggested from vendor history for the team to review and confirm for accountability
A booking proposal is digitising, not automating; own accounts and exceptions block the share that posts without a touch

risks: People confirm proposals without reading them
Wrong capital-versus-expense calls reach the balance sheet
Invoice data sent to an outside model needs a GDPR data processing agreement
research_questions: What share of invoices has no purchase order today?
How accurate are coding proposals on a back-test of last year's invoices?
Does the AFAS booking proposal already reach this accuracy without an external model?

tasks.short: Calculate amounts due, late-payment interest, discounts and open balances for suppliers and customers

today.trigger: A payment run, a customer dispute, an overdue customer or a supplier statement
steps: Export open items from AFAS to Excel
Calculate discounts and statutory commercial interest
Work out the balance after part-payments and credit notes
Check against the supplier statement
Enter the adjustments in AFAS
today.time_sinks: Part-payments and credit notes that do not match one-to-one

lenses.faster: AFAS calculates balances, discounts and statutory interest from open items. The Excel step disappears, and the bookkeeper checks the outliers only.
lenses.autonomous: A nightly job computes balances and interest and flags differences against supplier statements.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made much more often: whether to charge statutory interest to late customers, now checked weekly instead of hardly ever. Demand would grow, but the Credit and Collections Officer decides per customer.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss the Excel interest sheets. The bookkeepers want more time to talk with suppliers about real differences.
lenses.options: Charging interest or waiving it depends on the customer relationship. A side-by-side scenario helps the Credit and Collections Officer decide.
lenses.altitude: Their week shifts from calculating to explaining differences. The decision rights stay with the Credit and Collections Officer and the Controller.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: preparing interest and settlement proposals (learn the collection policy)

tasks.human_edge: Seeing when a calculated amount is right on paper but wrong commercially, such as a disputed delivery or a promised discount not in the system.
tasks.pattern_why: Interest, discount and balance arithmetic follow fixed formulas and rates.

in_practice.trigger: A nightly run, or a supplier statement received
steps: Pull open items and payments from AFAS
Compute balances, discounts and statutory interest
Compare with the supplier statement
Flag differences above tolerance
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper reviews flagged differences. Interest invoices to customers need approval from the Credit and Collections Officer.
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS open-item history and a difference report

evidence.claim: Balance, discount and interest calculation is standard ERP functionality
A large company may not agree payment terms over 30 days with a small supplier

risks: Wrong payment terms in the master data give wrong amounts at scale
Charging interest automatically could damage customer relationships
research_questions: How many hours a month go into Excel balance and interest calculations?
Are payment terms complete and correct in AFAS for all suppliers and customers?
Does Noordhaven want to charge statutory interest at all, and to whom?

tasks.short: Prepare payment batches to Rabobank for suppliers, agencies, taxes and utilities

today.trigger: The weekly payment run, and VAT and wage-tax due dates
steps: Select approved invoices that are due in AFAS
Split agency invoices between the g-rekening and the normal account
Check IBANs and look for duplicates
Create the batch and upload it to Rabobank
Get two signatures and approve
drudgery: Calculating the g-rekening split by hand
today.time_sinks: Agency invoices and last-minute urgent payments

lenses.faster: The payment run selects due items, computes the g-rekening share from agency invoices, and flags IBAN changes, duplicates and IBAN-name check warnings. The bookkeeper checks the flags and the totals.
lenses.autonomous: The weekly date starts the run. Selection and batch creation run on their own, and two people approve in Rabobank.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: paying small suppliers within 30 days, checked each run rather than at audit. Demand for it would not grow; it is a legal floor.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss the g-rekening sums. The bookkeepers want more time to look into the IBAN warnings that could be fraud.
lenses.options: In tight cash weeks, two or three payment scenarios (pay all, hold larger non-urgent invoices) change the Controller's decision.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper prepares and checks the run; the Controller and Finance Director decide timing in tight weeks. They gain the right to block a payment on a fraud flag.
reach: Payroll Specialist: checking wage-tax payments and agency payment-behaviour statements (learn ketenaansprakelijkheid)

tasks.human_edge: Spotting payment fraud: a changed IBAN with a plausible email, or a name mismatch the payee explains away. Confirming after a warning moves the risk to Noordhaven.
tasks.pattern_why: Selection, split percentages and duplicate and IBAN checks are rules; approval stays with people.

in_practice.trigger: Weekly payment date, or a tax due date
steps: Select approved, due invoices
Compute the g-rekening share per agency invoice
Flag IBAN changes, duplicates and small suppliers past 30 days
Create the SEPA batch for Rabobank
Two people approve after the IBAN-name check
in_practice.human_gate: Two-person approval of every batch in Rabobank, plus a bookkeeper decision on each flag
data_needed: Agency g-rekening data and payment-behaviour statements
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS payment batch history and Rabobank approval log

evidence.claim: Noordhaven can be liable for agencies' unpaid wage tax and VAT and limits this by paying part into the g-rekening
Banks check payee name against IBAN; a payer who confirms after a warning is not blocked
Maximum 30-day term toward small suppliers for large companies

risks: A wrong g-rekening percentage leaves Noordhaven liable for agency taxes
Approvers wave the batch through without reading it
research_questions: What g-rekening percentage do the three agencies use, and is it on the invoice?
How many IBAN-name check warnings came up in the last quarter, and how were they handled?
How many small suppliers were paid after 30 days last year?

tasks.short: Match bank statements, agency hours and Excel lists against AFAS ledgers and clear differences

today.trigger: The daily bank import and the month-end close
steps: Import the CAMT.053 statement from Rabobank
Match payments to open items by hand where AFAS fails
Compare agency invoices with hours in the portals
Tick off Excel side lists against AFAS
Investigate and post the differences
today.time_sinks: Customer payments covering several invoices, and agency hours that differ from invoices

lenses.faster: AFAS matches bank lines on reference, IBAN, invoice number and amount. A script compares agency invoices with portal hours, and a model explains unmatched lines so the bookkeeper starts from a suggestion.
lenses.autonomous: The daily bank import starts the match. Only misses and hour differences above tolerance reach the bookkeeper.
lenses.ambitious: Agency invoices are checked against hours for every week for the first time, covering the 150 to 300 flex workers. Demand would grow in peak season.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss ticking lists. The bookkeepers want more time to resolve the real differences with the agencies.
lenses.options: Little; there is one true match.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the match rules and tolerances in AFAS and settles hour differences with the agencies.
reach: Accountant: bank and creditor reconciliation for month-end close (learn the close calendar)

tasks.human_edge: Working out what a customer meant with an unclear payment, and agreeing hour differences with the agency planner.
tasks.pattern_why: Bank matching and hour comparisons are rules (reference, IBAN, amount, tolerance). The model only helps explain leftovers.

in_practice.trigger: Daily CAMT.053 import, or weekly agency invoice
steps: AFAS auto-matches bank lines
A script compares agency invoice hours with portal hours
A model suggests explanations for unmatched lines
The bookkeeper resolves and posts
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper decides on every unmatched line and hour difference
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS bank match log and a difference register

evidence.claim: AFAS matches CAMT.053 lines on payment reference, IBAN, invoice number and oldest-first sums; misses go to a person
Let AP run with people on exceptions and log every decision with its data

risks: Tolerances set too loosely hide errors
The agency portals may not have usable exports
research_questions: What is the AFAS auto-match rate on Noordhaven's bank lines today?
Can the three agency portals export hours per worker per week?
How much did hour differences on agency invoices cost last year?

tasks.short: Answer supplier, customer and colleague questions about payment status and account balances

today.trigger: Email or phone call from a supplier, customer, site manager or the Credit and Collections Officer
steps: Read the question and find the relation in AFAS
Look up the invoice, approval status and payment date
Check the bank statement if paid
Write the answer by email
drudgery: Repeating the same 'when will you pay' answer
today.time_sinks: Invoices stuck in approval, where the answer means chasing someone first

lenses.faster: An agent reads the email, looks up the status in AFAS and drafts the answer. The bookkeeper checks and sends in under a minute.
lenses.autonomous: An email arriving in the AP mailbox starts it. The agent drafts the answer, and the bookkeeper approves each one before it goes.
lenses.ambitious: Site managers get answers on payment status for the first time without emailing Finance, through a Teams question. Demand would grow because they now hold back on asking.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss the repeated status emails. The bookkeepers want more time on the calls that solve a real problem.
lenses.options: Little; the facts give the answer.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper reviews drafts and handles disputes. They decide which question types can later go out without review.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: first-line answers to customers on open balances (learn the dispute process)

tasks.human_edge: Hearing frustration or a hidden dispute in a supplier email and knowing when to call instead of write.
tasks.pattern_why: Questions vary and the lookup steps differ per question; a person approves before anything is sent outside.

in_practice.trigger: New email in the AP or AR mailbox
steps: The agent classifies the question and identifies the relation
It looks up invoice, approval and payment status in AFAS
It drafts the reply in Outlook
The bookkeeper approves, edits or takes over
in_practice.human_gate: The bookkeeper approves every outgoing reply
in_practice.logs_to: Outlook sent items plus a note on the AFAS relation

evidence.claim: Payment-status questions answered from AFAS fit an agent with a human gate
43% say manual approval regularly delays payment, which drives status questions

risks: Sharing account data with the wrong person (GDPR, sole traders)
A wrong promised payment date damages trust
research_questions: How many status questions arrive per week, and what share is about stuck approvals?
Can the agent read AFAS approval status through the API with read-only rights?
Would suppliers accept a self-service status page instead?

tasks.short: Track overdue customer and supplier accounts, and loans or leases, so payments stay up to date

today.trigger: Weekly aging review and the month-end close
steps: Run the aging report in AFAS or Power BI
Mark overdue customers and missed supplier payments
Check lease and loan instalments against the schedule
Pass the list to the Credit and Collections Officer
drudgery: Building the aging list by hand in Excel
today.time_sinks: Merging AFAS data with notes on disputes and payment promises

lenses.faster: A daily rule set flags overdue items, missed instalments and broken payment promises in Power BI. The bookkeeper reviews the list instead of building it.
lenses.autonomous: The nightly AFAS refresh starts it. AFAS sends standard reminders on schedule, and exceptions go to the Credit and Collections Officer.
lenses.ambitious: A decision made far more often: holding or releasing customer orders based on daily overdue status instead of monthly. Demand would grow as the commercial team trusts it.
lenses.joy: Nobody will miss building aging lists. The bookkeepers want more time on the customers who need a conversation.
lenses.options: Little here; collection choices sit with the Credit and Collections Officer.
lenses.altitude: The bookkeeper owns the reminder rules and thresholds, and the Credit and Collections Officer keeps the customer decisions.
reach: Credit and Collections Officer: running the first two reminder rounds (learn the reminder wording and escalation)

tasks.human_edge: Knowing which overdue customer has a real dispute or a promise from the account manager, so a reminder would do harm.
tasks.pattern_why: Overdue status, schedules and reminder timing follow fixed rules on AFAS data.

in_practice.trigger: Nightly AFAS extract to Power BI
steps: Compute aging and missed instalments
Exclude items marked as disputed
AFAS sends standard reminders
Exceptions go to a queue for the bookkeeper and the Credit and Collections Officer
in_practice.human_gate: The Credit and Collections Officer decides on escalation, order holds and anything beyond the standard reminders
in_practice.logs_to: AFAS reminder history and Power BI snapshot

evidence.claim: Billing, interest and account status work fits deterministic software at autonomy 4

risks: Reminders sent to customers with an open dispute
Missing dispute flags make the list unreliable
research_questions: Are disputes and payment promises recorded in AFAS today, or in mailboxes?
What is days sales outstanding (DSO) now, and how much of it comes from slow follow-up?
Does the commercial team want order holds based on overdue status?
